findings.check: Process group of the executor is stopped after a timeout, a cancel, too much output or a server shutdown (REQ-010 section 5.6; extra check 1, the executor)
findings.title: On Windows stopGroup reports 'the group is gone' without stopping anything: the Claude Code process keeps running (and spending) after a timeout or a cancel
findings.where: tools/src/team/executors/proc.js lines 14-31 (process.kill(-pid, ...)), tools/src/team/executors/claude-cli.js lines 229-247 (stop) and 207-214 (detached: true)
findings.evidence: The code stops the group with process.kill(-pid, sig) and reads 'group gone' from the error code ESRCH (proc.js:16-19 and 26-28). A negative pid is a POSIX group address. Probe on this PC (win32, Node 22.23.4), script <scratch>/aud002/sec-team/procprobe.mjs importing the proc.js of the fixed copy: output 'platform win32 child alive before true' / 'kill(-pid,0) error code: ESRCH groupAlive: false' / 'stopGroup returned true after ms 0' / 'child really alive after stopGroup: true' / 'child alive after direct kill by exact pid: false' (the child was stopped by the probe itself by its exact pid). So stopGroup returns true at once, sends nothing to the process, and groupAlive says false while the process is alive. In run(), stopping.then(...) calls forceCloseSoon only if the process has exited or the group is stuck (claude-cli.js:242-245), and groupStuck is never set here, so after a timeout or a cancel the attempt waits for 'close' of a process that nobody stopped; the timeout (default 1,200,000 ms) and the cancel therefore do not end the model process. The tests of the group (exec-group.test.js) ran on ubuntu-24.04 only (check.yml:18), the code has no branch for win32 (grep process.platform|win32 in tools/src: no match).
findings.item: Q10 and REQ-010 section 5.6 (a process of an attempt does not outlive the attempt); the money ceiling of the project (the stop is the last guard of the cost)
findings.recommendation: In tools/src/team/executors/proc.js add a Windows branch: stop the tree of the process with taskkill /PID <pid> /T (then /F after the grace time) and answer groupAlive by asking whether the pid exists (process.kill(pid, 0)) plus the descendants, or run the child inside a Windows job object; do not return true from goneWithin when nothing was sent. Until then claude-cli.js check() should refuse a real run when process.platform is win32 (new E_ code, texts in language.js), so the gate of G2 cannot be passed on the PC that cannot stop the process. Add a test of the Windows branch that starts a sleeping child and requires it to be gone (a Windows runner in check.yml or a documented 'not checked on Windows').

findings.check: Permissions of the data folder and the journal ('closed to other users', README: folders 0700, files 0600; links not followed); extra check 1
findings.title: On Windows the mode bits 0700/0600, the owner check and O_NOFOLLOW do nothing, and the code neither says so nor checks the folder access list
findings.where: tools/src/team/home.js lines 90-97 (ownUid, isOwn), 160-167 and 246-275 (ensureHome, ensureModes, wider), files.js:12, journal.js:17, runner.js:49, engine/channel.js:99, executors/scripted.js:36 (O_NOFOLLOW); tools/README.md lines 251 and 493
findings.evidence: Probe on this PC (win32): mkdirSync(d, {mode: 0o700}) then chmodSync(d, 0o700) gives lstat mode 666; a file written with mode 0o600 has mode 666; typeof process.getuid is 'undefined' (so isOwn returns true for every owner: home.js:94-96); fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW is undefined (so NOFOLLOW is 0 in files.js, journal.js, runner.js and the flags of channel.js and scripted.js). Consequences read in the code: wider(st, 0o700) is true on every start, so every write command prints 'Права сужены до 0700' although chmod changed nothing, and the real protection is only whatever access list the folder inherits (the default under the user profile is the owner, the administrators and the system; a folder named in SAI_TEAM_HOME on another drive may be readable by other users). README line 493 builds the trust in the inbox and in the journal on 'the folders are 0700'. A link planted between the lstat and the open is not stopped by the flag on Windows (files.js readWorkFile compares dev and ino, which covers that read only).
findings.item: Q7 (the journal and the results are kept where an outsider does not read them); README section 'Rights' versus the files
findings.recommendation: In tools/README.md (line 251 and 493) say that the 0700/0600 guarantee holds on Linux and macOS only and that on Windows the folder must lie under the user profile. In tools/src/team/home.js: on win32 do not print the false 'narrowed' notice, and warn (or refuse, as E_HOME) when SAI_TEAM_HOME is outside the user profile folder; optionally set an owner-only access list with icacls on creation of <home>. Add a test for the win32 branch of ensureHome that does not depend on mode bits.

summary.main_point: On Linux and macOS the part is sound: no secret in code, tests or fixtures (all fakes), the server is loopback-only with Host, Origin, page key and access cookie (ISS-0122 holds), the page inserts only text, paths and names cannot leave the project folder, secrets in result files are refused and not rewritten, and a real model run cannot start without SAI_TEAM_REAL_RUNS=1 and a project budget (gate G2 holds). The weak point is Windows, the PC where the owner works now: the process stop does nothing (High) and the file permission model is not enforced or announced (Medium). ISS-0092 (Node version) is open and named, not repeated.
doubts: D1. The effect of the flags --restricted, --safe-mode and --permission-prompts none is taken from the design; --allowedTools lists Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep without a path limit, so the confinement to work/ rests wholly on --restricted in a real session (not checked).

D2. isDomain checks names only: a name an owner puts into SAI_TEAM_WEB_DOMAINS that resolves to a local address passes, and the deny list names only literal local hosts; whether WebFetch checks the resolved address was not checked. The allow list is set by the owner, so the risk is small.
D3. WebSearch stays for the Researcher without an allow list (ISS-0119 closed it for WebFetch only); data could in principle go out in a search query. Not tested, left as a doubt.
D4. The name of a result file is stored unmasked by design (pattern only); a prompt-injected model could put a short value into the name. Local journal only; not reported.
